classifications.label: General-audience animation
classifications.definition: Animation not specifically directed to children, including works for teens or adults.
classifications.impacts: Normal content policy checks apply; animation format alone is not a child-directed designation.
classifications.limitations: Depends on actual video intent, characters, themes and presentation.

classifications.label: Mixed audience (child-directed)
classifications.definition: Content directed to children among other audiences after applying the factors in the official guidance.
classifications.impacts: Treated as child-directed under the relevant legal framework.
classifications.limitations: Mixed audience is not synonymous with general audience.

classifications.label: Made for kids
classifications.definition: Content targeted at children based on purpose, subjects and other contextual factors.
classifications.impacts: Selected interactive, commerce and personalized advertising features can be disabled.
classifications.limitations: Children's ages and applicable laws differ by region; this is not legal advice.

classifications.label: Teen-directed general content
classifications.definition: Content intended for teens or older viewers rather than children under the relevant legal threshold.
classifications.impacts: May be treated as general audience when genuinely not child-directed.
classifications.limitations: A label such as 'girls' or 'teen' does not by itself establish YouTube's classification.

policy_dimensions.economic_relevance: Ads may still be contextual; revenue per view cannot be inferred.
One form of recurring native fan funding may not be available.
Community engagement and some paid live interactions are limited.
YouTube's own product merchandising features have content restrictions; independent external sales need separate review.
Templated, minimally altered or mass-produced videos may jeopardize monetization.
Platform reuse assessment and copyright licensing are separate checks.
A published video may earn full, limited or no ad revenue depending on context.
Public-interest discussion can qualify under some advertiser policies; no uniform political category RPM is claimed.

prohibited_shortcuts: Classify all animation as made for kids
Label ordinary teen-interest video as made for kids solely to reach children
Infer viewer age from names, photos or watching patterns
Promote deceptive or repetitive content as monetization-safe
Assign a policy penalty RPM without empirical data
Generate microtargeted political persuasion using demographic findings
rules: The facts above describe rules, not legal advice or estimates of creator income.
A restriction is not automatically a total ban on posting or a zero-revenue result.
Differentiate content-level flags from channel-level sanctions.
Audience size, topic volume and payout likelihood remain different quantities.
